headline: Approved RD6 conservation rules that allow minor structures, and adopted the zoning map as it stands.
summary: Members approved adding restrictions from three conservation easements to the RD6 zone. They also adopted the zoning map with its current height and lot coverage limits. The ordinance goes next to the Planning Board on November 18th, then to the City Council.
decisions: Approved adding the conservation easement restrictions on structures to the RD6 zone. No vote count was given.
Adopted the zoning map as it stands, with its 35-foot height limit and 30% lot coverage for the developable area. No vote count was given.
discussion: RD6 minor structures: Members discussed which small structures the conservation easements allow, such as footbridges and small platforms, and whether to cite the deeds or write out the allowed and not allowed uses.
Lot coverage on the 300-acre parcel: Members questioned whether the map's 30% lot coverage matched an earlier vote, and debated whether the shoreland areas should be limited to 20%.
Buffer distance: Members discussed whether the 50-foot buffer should be 100 feet, and removed a buffer reference from the general ordinance so all university buffer rules sit in one ordinance.
Future conservation overlays: Members asked how future citywide wetland and vernal pool rules would affect the parcel, and noted that the overlay ordinance is expected next year.
Master plan: Members asked whether a master plan would be needed for the parcel, and the university said it has no plans for development there now.
